theme: Log privacy: keeping personal data out of logs

terms.definition: Personal or secret information, such as an email address or a password, that must be protected.
terms.example: Never print sensitive data in a log.
terms.code:
let email = "mina@example.com"
let masked = String(email.prefix(1)) + "***"
print(masked)

terms.definition: Hiding part of a message, so the log shows a placeholder instead of the real value.
terms.example: Redaction replaces the email with a placeholder.

terms.definition: The option type whose values, such as public and private, control how a value in a log message is shown.
terms.example: Mark the user id private with OSLogPrivacy.
terms.code:
import os
let logger = Logger()
let id = 42
logger.info("id \(id, privacy: .private)")

video.title: Sensitive Data, Redaction & OSLogPrivacy | Day 238
video.description:
Learn to explain how to keep private data safe when you write logs: Sensitive Data, Redaction & OSLogPrivacy, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Sensitive Data - Personal or secret information, such as an email address or a password, that must be protected.
Redaction - Hiding part of a message, so the log shows a placeholder instead of the real value.
OSLogPrivacy - The option type whose values, such as public and private, control how a value in a log message is shown.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Sensitive Data, Redaction and OSLogPrivacy in English?

dialogue.title: Careful with that email
dialogue.setting: Reviewing a log line before merge

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I logged the user email to debug a login bug. Is that okay?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Careful. An email is sensitive data, and sensitive data must not leak into logs.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Emails, passwords, tokens and addresses. Anything that identifies a person.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So how do I keep the log useful?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use privacy options. OSLogPrivacy lets you mark a value as `.private` or `.public`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Like the `privacy` label in my log line?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. With `.private`, the log shows a placeholder instead of the email. That is redaction.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: For strings, yes. Numbers are public by default, so set OSLogPrivacy on purpose.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the user id number needs `.private` too?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Mark it, and redaction protects it when other people read the log.

dialogue.code:
import os
let log = Logger()
let email = "mina@example.com"
log.info("user \(email, privacy: .private)")
